id.description: Permanent opaque identifier. Never reused, never changed once assigned.

previous_slugs.description: Slugs this record used to have before being renamed. The build emits a redirect stub page at each old URL pointing at the current one, so old links keep working. Append the old slug here whenever you change `slug`, never remove an entry once added.

native.description: The name written in its own script(s), as found in a source.

designers.description: Points at person ids. The reverse ('typefaces by this person') is computed at build time, not hand-maintained on the person record. Empty only when no individual designer can be named - see `attribution`, required in that case (enforced by scripts/validate.js, not expressible in this schema alone).

unknown.description: Older form of status: unknown. Still accepted.

status.description: Why no individual is credited: unknown, anonymous (deliberately uncredited), collective (made by a group or community), foundry-only (credited to the organisation), lost (records did not survive).

note.description: Plain description of the attribution, e.g. "Credited to the foundry's in-house team".

attribution.description: Only set when designers is empty. Never set alongside a non-empty designers[] - enforced by scripts/validate.js.

era.description: Production technology. A list when the typeface exists in more than one, e.g. ["metal", "digital"].

languages.description: Languages the typeface was made for or documented as supporting, as stated in a source. Separate from scripts.

related_typefaces.description: This typeface's relation to another RTD typeface, e.g. {"id": "rtd-t-000012", "relation": "digitisation_of"}.

commissioned_by.description: Organisation(s) or person(s) that commissioned the typeface, only when a source states it.

unicode_compliant.description: False for digital fonts that map a script's glyphs onto non-standard code points (plain ASCII, PUA, or another script's block) instead of the script's real Unicode block, common in fonts made before a script was encoded. Omit when not established either way, don't assume true by default.

lc_naf.description: Library of Congress/NACO Authority File id.

worldcat_entity.description: OCLC WorldCat Entity id, the string after id.oclc.org/worldcat/entity/. Note: the WorldCat.org detail page for an entity currently prompts for a library-affiliated login to view, unlike the other authority files here, still worth recording as a cross-reference even though the page itself isn't always freely browsable.

external_ids.description: Informational cross-references only, one per authority file. Never usable as a sources entry.

type.description: What kind of document this is. Descriptive only.

language.description: Language of the source, as a BCP 47 tag (e.g. en, or, sat, hi, ar).

date.description: Publication date as given by the source (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD).

archive_url.description: An archived copy of url, e.g. on web.archive.org.

sources.description: Independent, verifiable sources. Must never be Wikidata, Wikipedia, or any Wikimedia project, enforced by scripts/validate.js.

contributed_by.description: Who submitted or substantially contributed this record's entry - distinct from the typeface's own designers[]. The first entry is treated as the record's citation author (see site-templates/shared.js buildCitations). Auto-filled with the submitter's GitHub username for issue-form submissions; add by hand when opening a PR directly, see CONTRIBUTING.md. Also powers the /contributors/ page. Omit entirely for records researched and entered by the registry's own maintainers - the citation falls back to the default maintainer credit in that case.

verification_status.description: Set to needs_verification when sources are thin or low-confidence rather than omitting the record entirely. Absent/'verified' means sources are considered solid.
